For me, the best thing for getting started is a gym buddy or an accountability partner of some sort. If you can find either of those, being regular will be probably 95% taken care of. At one point, I had a buddy start spamming me with texts until I could prove I was working out. Otherwise, I've been setting timers. When this timer goes off, I stop whatever I'm doing, put my gym clothes on, and start my warmup.

I've only ever really done weightlifting, so I couldn't give any advice on bodyweight vs. weights. However, I do know that the bodyweight guy got completely and hilariously demolished in this video. Stronglifts is a pretty good beginner routine, though. It's a variation of Starting Strength, which is pretty much the standard. The most important routine, however, is one you like, and can stick with. If you don't like your routine, you won't do it. Consistency is king. Someone with the worst routine on the planet, but is consistent, will still lap someone with the best routine, who never gets off the couch. Tortoise and the hair and all that.

Also, don't set lofty goals. You don't run the marathon by saying "I have x miles to go until I'm done". You just focus on putting one foot in front of the other. Just deal with that next step, over and over again, and before you know it, you're at the finish line. The same with weight lifting. You don't say "I'm going to lift a gorillion pounds, be in the Olympics, and set world records!", because you'll always be paying attention to how far away from those gorillion pounds you are, instead of paying attention to how far you've come. Set small goals. Like when I started, I couldn't even bench the bar. That's how scrawny I was. So that was my first goal. "I'm going to lift the bar", and then I did. Then my next goal became "I want to lift one plate!", and the weights on that bar slowly got bigger and bigger, and I got more and more excited. Next thing I knew, there was a plate on the bar. Today, that's not even my warmup weight. Eventually, just seeing your progress alone will be a massive rush, and will be enough to get yourself into the gym.
